subject: maths
chapter_title: Tales by Dots and Lines: The Balancing Act

concepts.title: Balance Point Property of Mean
concepts.definition: The arithmetic mean acts as the central fulcrum of a numerical dataset where the sum of deviation distances for values below the mean equals the sum of deviation distances for values above it.
concepts.key_idea: Mean balances total deviation distances of observations on either side.
question_patterns: verify if the mean balances distances on both sides in Grade 8 statistics
check the balance of distances on the left and right of the mean
explain how the mean represents the centre of a dot plot
determine if a given number is the balance point mean of a dataset
show that the sum of distances below the mean equals those above

solution_steps.explain: sum the differences between the mean and every observation smaller than the mean
sum the differences between every observation greater than the mean and the mean
verify that total left distance equals total right distance

concepts.title: Mean Transformation by Addition or Subtraction
concepts.definition: When a constant value is added to or subtracted from every item in a dataset, the mean shifts by that exact same constant value.
concepts.key_idea: Adding or subtracting a fixed value to all entries alters the mean by that same value.
question_patterns: find the new mean when every value is increased by a constant in Class 8 data
calculate the modified mean if all data entries are decreased by a fixed number
what is the new average when a shift is added to each observation
determine the correct average after subtracting shoe height from all student measurements
compute the updated mean after adding a fixed value to every entry

solution_steps.action: add the shift to the original mean
solution_steps.explain: shifting every value by a constant shifts the mean by the same constant
a positive shift increases the mean while a negative shift decreases it by the same magnitude
the new mean equals the original mean plus the constant shift applied uniformly to all entries

concepts.title: Mean Transformation by Multiplication
concepts.definition: When every element in a dataset is scaled by multiplying with a fixed constant factor, the arithmetic mean of the dataset is multiplied by that same factor.
concepts.key_idea: Scaling all data entries by a constant factor scales the mean proportionally.
question_patterns: find the new mean when all values in a dataset are doubled
calculate the scaled average after multiplying every entry by a factor
what is the new mean if each observation is scaled by a constant
determine the average when every data point is multiplied by a fixed number
compute the modified mean after scaling all scores

solution_steps.action: multiply the original mean by the scaling factor
solution_steps.explain: scaling every observation by a factor scales the overall mean by the same factor
a factor greater than 1 enlarges the mean, a factor between 0 and 1 shrinks it, and a negative factor reverses its sign
the new mean equals the original mean multiplied by the constant factor applied to all entries

concepts.title: Finding a Missing Value from the Mean
concepts.definition: An unknown observation in a dataset is found by computing the required total sum from the given mean and count, then subtracting the sum of all known observations.
concepts.key_idea: Subtract the sum of known entries from the total product of mean and count.
question_patterns: find the missing value in a dataset given the overall mean and count
calculate the smudged weight when average weight and other entries are known
what is the unknown observation if the mean of n numbers is given
determine the missing score given average score and sum of remaining scores
compute the unknown value y given the dataset mean and other entries

solution_steps.explain: multiply mean by count to find required total sum

solution_steps.action: subtract known sum from total sum
solution_steps.explain: the difference gives the missing value

solution_steps.action: verify the missing value is consistent
solution_steps.explain: check that adding the missing value to the known sum reproduces the target total sum, confirming correctness

concepts.title: Correcting Mean for Erroneous Data Entries
concepts.definition: To rectify a mean calculated with an error, obtain the initial sum, adjust for the difference between incorrect and actual entries, and divide by total item count.
concepts.key_idea: Adjust initial aggregate total for observational errors and re-divide by count.
question_patterns: find the correct average when one observation was recorded incorrectly
calculate the rectified mean after subtracting an overcount error
what is the true mean when a data entry was misread by a given amount
determine the adjusted average harvest when one count was wrong
compute the correct mean after fixing a measurement mistake

solution_steps.explain: multiply initial mean by count
subtract the excess error amount from initial sum

solution_steps.action: divide correct total sum by count
solution_steps.explain: find rectified mean

concepts.title: Mean of Frequency Distribution Data
concepts.definition: The mean of tabular frequency data is computed by dividing the total sum of value-frequency products by the aggregate frequency count.
concepts.key_idea: Divide the aggregate value product sum by the total number of entries.
question_patterns: find the average family size from a frequency distribution table
calculate the mean from a frequency table of given values and frequencies
what is the average score when observations have specified frequencies
determine the mean of grouped frequency data in Class 8 statistics
compute the mean using sum of frequency products over total frequency

solution_steps.action: divide total product sum by total frequency
solution_steps.explain: divide aggregate sum of all values by total number of items

solution_steps.action: verify the product sum was computed correctly
solution_steps.explain: ensure each value was multiplied by its frequency and the products were summed across all categories

solution_steps.action: state the final mean of the frequency distribution
solution_steps.explain: the ratio of total product sum to total frequency gives the average value of the grouped data

concepts.title: Median of Frequency Distribution Data
concepts.definition: The median in a frequency table is identified by finding running cumulative frequencies to determine the entry positioned at the exact midpoint of the ordered dataset.
concepts.key_idea: Locate the middle data position using cumulative sum of frequencies.
question_patterns: find the median family size from a given frequency table
determine the median value using cumulative frequencies
calculate the median position and value for a frequency distribution
what is the median of data presented in a frequency distribution
how to locate the central value in a frequency table

solution_steps.explain: sum all frequencies in the table
find N/2 position for even total or (N+1)/2 for odd total
cumulate frequencies from smallest value up to locate the category matching the central position

concepts.title: Spreadsheet Formulas SUM and AVERAGE
concepts.definition: Spreadsheet software uses cell range expressions like SUM(Start:End) and AVERAGE(Start:End) to automatically calculate total sums and arithmetic averages across rows or columns.
concepts.key_idea: Cell range syntax with colon notation evaluates aggregate sum or mean.
question_patterns: write the spreadsheet formula to calculate the total marks in a row
what cell formula computes the average score across a subject column
determine the spreadsheet syntax to sum cells B3 to G3
find the correct formula for average of cells B7 through D7
identify the spreadsheet formula for row totals and column averages

solution_steps.action: identify row or column cell range
solution_steps.explain: determine starting and ending cell coordinates
format formula starting with equals sign, function name, and cell range in parentheses
confirm the computed result matches the expected total or average by checking the highlighted cell value

concepts.title: Line Graph Interpretation and Trend Analysis
concepts.definition: Line graphs plot sequential data points connected by line segments to depict variations, comparative trends, and rates of change over continuous time intervals.
concepts.key_idea: Line segment slopes highlight temporal changes and multi-series comparisons.
question_patterns: interpret maximum temperature trends over months using a line graph
compare space object launches across different years using line plots
identify peak rainfall months from a line graph of multiple cities
what information does a line graph convey about time series data
analyze trends and rate of increase in line graph representations

solution_steps.action: read data points and line steepness

solution_steps.action: compare multiple series and summarize the trend
solution_steps.explain: when several lines are plotted together, contrast their slopes and peaks to draw comparative conclusions about the data over time

concepts.title: Infographics and Activity Time Strips
concepts.definition: Infographics and activity strips map categorical data, regional preference scales, or daily time allocations visually through proportional color-coded segments.
concepts.key_idea: Color-coded visual strips represent duration and categorical distributions.
question_patterns: analyze an activity strip to estimate time spent on daily tasks

solution_steps.action: read color legend and block scale
